Mandok Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mándok, Hungary

Not demolished. Mándok's Jewish community is first recorded in 1770, with 7 residents; it grew to 51 by 1840, 358 by 1880, and 400 by 1930. Following the 1868 Schism in Hungarian Jewry, the community joined the Orthodox stream, building a synagogue in 1861 alongside a mikveh, school, and rabbi's house. In 1944, Mándok's Jews were taken to the Kisvárda Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz on May 29; 20 women and 18 men later returned as survivors. The synagogue itself was demolished in 1963. The cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1849, its newest to 1957.
